identity.trade: Pelts and venison: a hunters' hold on the edge of the wild, where every hunter carries a wolf-tooth token.

greeting: Quiet in the lodge. Pelts are drying and so are tempers.
Brackenmoor is hunters and pelts. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Pelts are up in price and down in number. Do the sum yourself.
A lost dog came back with a collar nobody has seen. Silver, and warm.
Wolves came down from the east ridge at noon last week. They have learned the stones are tired.

opinions.gethin_dobbin: I would trust Gethin with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Dawn hunt. If you are coming, keep quiet.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. I would say nice day, but it is not, and you would know.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
Brackenmoor is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Hunters tell the same stories each night, bigger each time. The stag is now a monster.
A man paid for a room and asked which way the stones face. I put him by the stairs.
A hunting party found a camp with a cold fire and no tracks.
The Hunters' Lodge drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.cressa_fothergill: Cressa undercuts me. I forgive Cressa. Mostly.

time.evening: Back from the trail. Boots wet, bags light.

dialogue.aside: Take something. Anything. No, a bigger something. I insist.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
Boots light, bow dry, mouth shut. That is the code.
rumour: Broadheads, knives, trap springs. I sharpen what bites.
The forge hums when the stones dim. Not loud. Enough to notice.
A fox with a white tail ran through the lodge yard at noon and the dogs did not bark.

opinions.folke_wakeley: Folke has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Folke.
opinions.norah_graye: Norah undercuts me. I forgive Norah. Mostly.

time.night: Dark wood. Keep a fire and keep your eyes open.

greeting: Take your time. Touch nothing you cannot afford.
Strangers in Brackenmoor get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Bowstring, bait and bandages. A hunter's list is short and urgent.
Sold three lanterns today. People are afraid of the dark again.
The best tracker in town came back from the ridge in silence and has not hunted since.
The Hunters' Lodge has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.cressa_fothergill: Cressa undercuts me. I forgive Cressa. Mostly.
opinions.olwen_wrenn: I would trust Olwen with a purse. A small one.

time.rain: Rain keeps the deer in and the hunters out. Tempers are shorter than the days.

dialogue.aside: Take something. Anything. No, a bigger something. I insist.

greeting: Loaf, bun, or the heel nobody wants? The heel is free.
Welcome to Brackenmoor. Mind the Hunters' Lodge. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: The oven runs hot because the town runs hungry.
A flock of ravens follows the hunters now. They take nothing. They wait.
The huntmaster pays for news of dens, and double for news of wasps.

opinions.isolt_skerrit: Isolt and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.morning: Dawn hunt. If you are coming, keep quiet.

dialogue.aside: You came. I am delighted. I have rehearsed this expression.

greeting: If it hurts it is working. If it does not hurt, you overpaid.
Soft voice. The wood listens.
rumour: Fever in two households. Nothing the stones can mend.
Wolves came down off the ridge in daylight. Daylight. Bold as sheep.

opinions.norah_graye: Norah is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.evening: Back from the trail. Boots wet, bags light.

dialogue.aside: Ha! Friend! Pull up a stool, I have a story and half a loaf.

greeting: State your business and keep your hands where I can see them.
The Hunters' Lodge is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Nine spears for the whole wall. I count them like sheep.
Pelts are thick this winter. The cold came early and does not feel natural.

opinions.wadsworth_sedge: Wadsworth knows the trade. I will say that for Wadsworth.

time.night: Dark wood. Keep a fire and keep your eyes open.

dialogue.aside: Friend. I have a deal. A small one, and only a little crooked.

greeting: Halt. Ah. Not a thief. Carry on.
Game does not come to the loud. Neither do I.
rumour: A stone by the gate flickered at midnight. I wrote it down. Nobody reads it.
Hides from the north are cut wrong. Not by a hand. By something with claws.
If trade slows, Brackenmoor feels it first. If it speeds up, Brackenmoor feels it last.

opinions.freya_hazelden: Freya knows the trade. I will say that for Freya.
opinions.ingram_stannard: Ingram works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain keeps the deer in and the hunters out. Tempers are shorter than the days.

dialogue.aside: Whatever you need, friend. Ask. I will not make you ask twice.

greeting: Evening. Stones are lit, gate is shut, I am cold.
Folk come to Brackenmoor for hunters and pelts. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Captain says it is nothing. Captain also says that about rain.
A hart stood in the lodge yard at dawn and left a pile of shed antlers. A gift or a warning.

opinions.neville_ledger: Neville lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.wadsworth_sedge: Wadsworth knows the trade. I will say that for Wadsworth.

time.morning: Dawn hunt. If you are coming, keep quiet.

dialogue.aside: You look tired, friend. I will not lie. Rest.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
First time in Brackenmoor? The Hunters' Lodge is the place to start.
rumour: Winters were colder, summers longer, and the wolves stayed home. Or so I choose to remember.
A stag with a broken antler still leads the herd. Nobody dares hunt him.
Ask in Brackenmoor who built the Hunters' Lodge and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.ingram_stannard: Ingram lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.evening: Back from the trail. Boots wet, bags light.

dialogue.aside: What did you see on the road? Tell me every bit. I will keep the details.

greeting: You are somebody's grandchild. I can tell by the walk.
You will hear Brackenmoor before you see it. Ask at the Hunters' Lodge.
rumour: When I was young the stones sang at dusk. Now they hum, like someone ill.
Brackenmoor lives by hunters and pelts. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.maeve_goodrich: Maeve lives next door and hears everything I do.

dialogue.aside: Forgive me. It has been a long week and a longer day. Still, it is good to see you.

greeting: Step light. If something is watching, it is the wood, and the wood is patient.
rumour: A stag stood in the road this morning and did not move. Looked at me like I owed it something.
Folk say Brackenmoor was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

dialogue.aside: Friend! I have a plan. It is a terrible plan. It is going to be wonderful.

greeting: Mind your step. Traps are cheaper than doctors.
rumour: The foxes are leaving. Not dying, leaving. They know something.
Every few years Brackenmoor has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

rumour: Orders for broadheads doubled. Nobody hunts that much.
